messages.author: 327a8e5641d73ebe
messages.subject: subsetting individual chromosomes
parts:
Hi,

I am new to R/QTL and have imported data from QTL Cartographer into R.
My chromosomes were named chr-1, chr-2,...,chr-5 in my original files
but were renamed by R to be:

levels(numleavout.em$chr)
[1] "-1" "-2" "-3" "-4" "-5"

when I try to plot my LOD scores one chromosome at a time, I get the
following error:

plot(numleavout.em,chr=-1)
Error in plot.scanone(numleavout.em, chr = -1) :
Chromosome(s) to plot were not matched to those in the scanone
output.

The plot error suggests I am using the wrong chromosome names but the
levels output suggests I am using the correct chromosome names. How
should I be subsetting the individual chromosomes?

Thanks

messages.author: f388084a0de67b60
messages.subject: Re: subsetting individual chromosomes
parts:
Yes, things are looking a little strange.
It's best to call the chromosomes "1", "2", etc.
"chr1", "chr2", etc. should work, but "chr-1", "chr-2" seem
to reveal a bug.

I think in reading in the data, we look for things like "chr1",
"chr2" and then strip off the "chr" part. But if they're labeled
"chr-1" then end up being labelled with negative numbers, which
causes problems later on, as in subsetting, you can generally use
-1 to mean plotting all chromosomes *except* chr 1.

If you go into your cartographer files and replace things like
"chr-1" with "chr1", everything should work.

And in future versions, hopefully I'll remember to fix this.

karl
